item.title: The secret of 'strange metals' may lie in quantum statistics, not collisions
item.description: In an ordinary metal, electrons behave like well-defined particles that occasionally bump into imperfections or vibrations of the crystal. Many materials with strong electron–electron interactions, including the copper-oxide (cuprate) superconductors, break these rules. In these "strange metals," electrical resistance rises in a straight line with temperature over a very wide range. Electrons seem to lose their momentum at the fastest rate quantum mechanics allows, the so-called Planckian limit. What causes this is still an open question. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Bacteria have many strategies for defending themselves against antibiotics. Some destroy the drug, others pump it out or alter its target. A team at the University of Geneva (UNIGE) has discovered how Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a bacterium responsible for infections that are often difficult to treat, very rapidly restricts the entry of imipenem, an antibiotic reserved for the most critical cases. item.title: More than 1,700 bee species are unique to islands, first global assessment finds
item.description: More than 1,700 bee species are found only on islands, the first global checklist of island bees shows. If you like bees and island destinations, the best places to visit are in the Mediterranean. Islands like Sicily and Cyprus are where you find the highest diversity of bee species in the world.
